pr_title: Modify mem_usage2 module callback to enable to take sample_size argument
pr_body:
This is useful for approximating size computation of complex module types.
Note that the mem_usage2 callback is new and has not been released yet, which is why we can modify it.
pr_comments: @redis/core-team please approve an additional argument to a new module callback not yet released.

issue_context.title: [MODULES API] RedisModuleTypeMemUsageFunc should accept a samples argument
issue_context.body: In the context of being called via `MEMORY USAGE`, the optional `SAMPLES` argument or its default value should be respected by modules, when applicable in the context of the data structure in question.

review_comments:
i think you're missing some update to the documentation of the `mem_usage2` field in module.c.
we can probably refer to the documentation of the MEMORY USAGE command, and i think we need to state that a value of 0 means infinite.
`memoryCommand` already sets samples num to inf in case of 0, so sample_size arg in moduleTypeMemUsageFunc2 will always be >0.

ok... so we must document that....
i.e that's different than the other public documentation of this feature...

alternatively, maybe that's less intuitive for a developer, and it's better to reflect the user input as is?
now we have a chance to change that (we won't be able to do that after we release that API).

i don't currently have a clear preference, as long as it's documented.

Well, I think that the assumption that 0 means inf should be in Redis level only, and when implementing the size computation method by a module, developer should know nothing about this assumption, and use it as a real samples num, so we can keep doing the transformation in `memoryCommand`, and assume `objectComputeSize` receives the real sample_size.

ok, not documenting it can't cause any harm, worse case, someone will implement code that handles the value of 0, and i'll be dead code.
so the only damage is some confusion for the module author.
